Subject: Initial DPA intake / scope clarification + eSign preference

Janet —

Thanks for the quick intro. We’re excited to move Eden Health through our privacy onboarding so you can start the pilot. A few asks to kick this off so Legal/IT at both sides can align: 

1) Can you please share your current DPA template and the latest subprocessor inventory? (I attached our Redwood DPA template for reference.)
2) Do you have an eSign preference (DocuSign vs Adobe Sign)? We typically send a shared DocuSign envelope for DPAs but can accommodate Adobe Sign if you require it.
3) High-level scope: please confirm the product/services in-scope and whether any customer data will be considered regulated health information (PHI). If PHI may be exchanged, flag it now so we can route to our security/compliance reviewer.
4) Transfers: Are there EU-origin data flows we should model (e.g., EU patients)? If yes, confirm whether you expect SCCs, BCRs, or another mechanism.

Proposed timeline: if we get your DPA + subprocessor list this week, Karthik and Laura will return a short redline and proposed counter within 48 business hours.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_template_v1.pdf (Redwood standard DPA)

Best,
Monica Patel

Monica —

Thanks, attaching our DPA and current subprocessor CSV. We prefer DocuSign for corporate agreements (we use Adobe Sign only in limited cases).

Quick answers:
- Product scope: pilot will include patient scheduling & anonymized usage telemetry. No PHI will be sent to Redwood during the pilot, but we do expect limited patient identifiers during integration testing (names + MRN) — will require careful scoping.
- Transfers: Some telemetry originates from EU clinics. We use SCCs today; our legal team will want SCCs or an EU Addendum on top of the DPA.

Attachments: Eden_DPA_vA.docx, eden_subprocessors.csv

Janet Singh

Subject: Re: Initial DPA intake / scope clarification + eSign preference (internal)

Looping internal thread with my read of Eden's DPA and the subprocessor list. Notes / proposed positions:

- EU transfers: Eden will expect SCCs. We should be prepared to accept the SCC framework and provide a short EU Addendum that references our subprocessors and dataflow. Ops will need to confirm which infra hosts EU telemetry.
- Subprocessors: eden_subprocessors.csv lists two monitoring providers and a logging vendor (LogStream). Two questions: 1) can we provide a monthly attestation of subcontractor changes rather than ad-hoc notices? 2) do we allow Eden to terminate for a material subprocessor change (reasonable to push negotiation here).
- PHI: they're flagging limited identifiers during integration testing. If PHI is present, we need to engage Security for tighter controls and possible controls addendum. This could change timelines.
- eSign: DocuSign is fine. We should propose shared envelope with acknowledgement page listing subprocessors + dataflow summary.

Action items I recommend:
1) Draft a one-page EU Addendum (SCCs + list of subprocessors) for Eden to sign alongside DPA.
2) Prepare a short attestation template for monthly subprocessor updates.
3) Ask Janet to call out which endpoints/file stores might receive test identifiers.

I’ll draft the redline highlights and upload.

-Karthik

Attachment: redline_notes_monica_karthik.pdf (internal redline and negotiation plan)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Janet Singh <janet.singh@edenhealth.com>, Eden Health Legal <legal@edenhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial DPA intake / scope clarification + eSign preference

Janet —

Thanks for the materials and the clarifications. Short summary and proposed path so Legal can align quickly: 

1) eSign: DocuSign works for us. We will prepare a shared DocuSign envelope (Redwood as sender) and include an acknowledgement page listing the in-scope services and the subprocessor matrix. Please confirm Eden’s signer for Legal (name + email) and whether you require IP/integration sign-off before countersignature.

2) EU transfers: we accept SCCs. We will produce a concise EU Addendum that references the SCCs and enumerates the subprocessors that process EU telemetry. This Addendum is designed to be signed alongside the DPA and will not require a separate DocuSign envelope.

3) Subprocessor notifications: we propose a monthly attestation model (Redwood will notify Eden within 30 days of material additions) and agree to provide an up-to-date CSV via a shared Drive link. If Eden needs unilateral termination rights specifically for certain classes of subprocessor changes, flag which classes and we can escalate to Legal.

4) PHI/identifiers during test: please confirm which endpoints and sample data flows will carry patient identifiers during integration testing (we treat those as sensitive and will lock down access until Security signs off).

Next steps / timeline: 
- I’ll share the DocuSign envelope and the Redwood EU Addendum by EOD tomorrow. 
- If Eden returns the DPA with comments, we will aim to provide redline responses within 48 business hours.

DocuSign link (will be live when envelope sent): https://docusign.com/ENVELOPE/ABC123

If this plan looks good, please reply with the Legal signer and the testing endpoints so we can keep to the pilot start date.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
